title: The Lady on the Hill is El Paso's most haunted location
excerpt: Under the Franklin Mountains, El Paso High School, known as “The Lady on the Hill,” is the city’s oldest working high school and has gained a reputation for being the most haunted place in El Paso.
content:
Originally established as Central High School in 1865, El Paso High School stands out among the sea of other schools with its Greco-Roman style architecture and its long, haunting and fascinating history.

Under the Franklin Mountains, El Paso High School, known as “The Lady on the Hill,” is the city’s oldest working high school and has gained a reputation for being the most haunted place in El Paso.

The school opened for operation in 1916 and was designed by famous architect Henry C. Trost. El Paso High has three stories, an elevated basement and elaborate tunnels. It is also a place where students and faculty have claimed to have seen objects being thrown off shelves, heard footsteps or chatter in the halls or have even seen ghosts.

One of the most popular urban legends surrounds a young woman who was rumored to have jumped from a balcony in the 1920s. Students claimed to have seen a woman walking the halls or stairway near the balcony she allegedly jumped from, wearing a white dress.

In 1985, a class yearbook photo strengthened this legend. Pictured in the yearbook, in the second row on the right, a blurry figure appearing to be a young woman, nicknamed “Ghost Girl,” wearing a white dress, connected her to the girl believed to be walking the halls.

According to ghost hunters, Haunted Room Co., nobody could identify the girl and the school faculty at the time had no recollection of the girl in the photo negative, yet she showed up in the developed photo.

Ghost Girl remains a mystery, and her alleged appearances have become a part of El Paso High School’s haunted folklore. 

There are other haunted spaces in the high school worth exploring, Like the underground tunnels beneath the school. 

During World War II, the basement and the tunnels under the school allegedly served as an overflow morgue for soldiers and a temporary holding facility for bodies during the Spanish Flu. Those underground spaces have also become part of the school’s ghost lore.  

According to Ghost Texas, a paranormal investigation team that explores haunting in Texas, students who have explored the basement have claimed to find sealed classrooms in perfect condition boarded up in a hasty fashion. More footsteps and laughter can be heard from the hallways that lead to the basement adding to the eerie energy of the basement. 

A story from a former teacher in the 1980s detailed an incident where two doors leading toward the tunnels suddenly flew open during basketball practice. According to the teacher, the doors opened again after students placed a bench in front of them, sending the team rushing from the building. 

Students have also claimed to hear cheering and fanfare in the empty auditorium above the tunnels, sudden temperature drops and foggy mists in the hallways leading to the basement. 

Many of these stories have been passed down through word of mouth, and there is very little documented evidence, but the haunted legends of the school are widely believed in the city. 

In a 2024 KVIA survey of El Paso’s most haunted locations, El Paso ranked El Paso High School at number one, and the school received more mentions from residents than any other location.  

It’s long history, historical significance and generational folklore have earned El Paso High School a reputation for being one of the most haunted high schools in the United States.
